subject: Operational exception request — Clearsail pilot uptime target and commercial terms
messages:
From: Alvaro Mendes <alvaro@clearsail.health>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 28 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot SLO request: 99.5 uptime and credit handling

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for the demo earlier this week — the team at Clearsail is excited to move forward with the 90‑day pilot. Before we sign the SOW we have one operational ask from our reliability team: for an initial pilot we need a temporary uptime target of 99.5% (vs Redwood's standard 99.95%) and a reduced service credit exposure while we exercise the integration.

Specifically: can Redwood accept a 99.5% uptime SLO for the 90‑day pilot period, and cap service credits tied to that pilot at no more than 5% of the monthly invoice for the pilot months? We are comfortable with a stricter target once the pilot completes.

This will determine internal approval on our end — procurement copied. Please advise on whether Redwood can agree and whether there are any commercial offsets (discounts, credits, or termination rights) you expect.

Best,
Alvaro Mendes
Head of Platform Engineering
Clearsail Health

Quick summary of internal asks I have for approval:
- Acceptance of a temporary 99.5% uptime SLO strictly for the 90‑day pilot window.
- A cap on service credits for pilot months (Clearsail asked for 5% cap).
- A commercial concession: Clearsail is requesting a one‑time onboarding discount to offset the relaxed SLO; they asked what we can do here.

I attached the draft SOW with proposed redlines and an initial economics workbook that shows credit exposure at different thresholds. Marissa / Jonas / Ben — can you weigh in with what we can authorize at our level vs what needs exec signoff?

Subject: Re: Pilot SLO request: 99.5 uptime and credit handling

Thanks Lauren and Alvaro.

Commercial view: I support a pilot‑only SLO adjustment to 99.5% provided we get a few commercial protections. Proposed guardrails:
- Pilot window = 90 days from first production traffic.
- Service credit cap for pilot months = 3% of the monthly invoice (lower than Clearsail's 5% ask).
- We offer a 15% onboarding discount for the first two months (one‑time commercial offset).
- At pilot completion we revert to standard SLO 99.95% unless both sides agree to extend.

Rationale: the discount is limited and temporary; the credit cap reduces downside while still being meaningful to the customer. Anything above this will require VP signoff.

Jonas — if legal can scope this as a limited operational exception with a sunset clause (90 days) and explicit waiver of ongoing credits beyond the pilot, we can proceed to signature. Ben — please confirm the economics impact is acceptable.

Marissa Cole
VP, Sales Operations
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Pilot SLO request: 99.5 uptime and credit handling

Laurens / Marissa / Alvaro — I've redlined the SOW to reflect the pilot exception and a sunset clause. Key legal points:
- Exception is explicitly pilot‑only (90 days). After pilot we revert to standard SLO and remedy terms.
- Service credits for pilot months will be capped at 3% of the monthly invoice (commercial agreed).
- Limited liability paragraph: we will not change data governance or indemnities for this exception — both sides keep standard warranties.
- Add an explicit schedule that lists the pilot start date trigger and measurement methodology (monitoring window, rolling window calculations).

I uploaded the redline to the shared Drive and started a DocuSign envelope for signature; see link below. I recommend Clearsail confirm the pilot start trigger language.

Subject: Re: Pilot SLO request: Pilot credit exposure and finance recommendation

Quick finance readout on the proposed guardrails:
- With a 3% monthly credit cap and an average expected pilot invoice of $120k/month, max credit exposure per month = ~$3.6k. Across 3 months that's ~$10.8k — within acceptable bounds for this account and the expected expansion upside.
- The 15% onboarding discount for months 1–2 reduces revenue by approx $36k total; combined with the credit exposure the total shortfall is ~ $46.8k. That's acceptable if Clearsail signs a 12‑month committed minimum after pilot or we secure a modest commitment (preferred).

Recommendation: approve pilot exception with the 3% cap and 15% discount conditional on:
1) A commitment to a 12‑month minimum or an agreed follow‑on commercial review at pilot end; OR
2) A prepayment / deposit covering month 1 (optional but preferred).

If legal wants different risk language, flag to me and I will re‑run the numbers.

Ben Carter
Director, Finance — Commercial Deals
ben_carter@redwood.com
